answer: Coordinated Pulse Window: each identity may act only during a randomly assigned slot, and slot assignments depend on prior participation density, so clusters of new agents collide instead of spreading. An attacker's flood lands in a narrow geologically stable window, like basalt forming under pressure, forcing retries. Each retry consumes a fresh attestation fee plus a gale of delayed throughput, so scaling the sybil set multiplies per-identity cost rather than amortizing it.
